evidence.claim: Jokowi asked ministers and related agency heads to stop raising postponement of the 2024 election or extension of his presidential term, saying the process had to stay constitutional.
evidence.title: Presiden minta jajaran kabinet tak lagi suarakan isu penundaan pemilu
evidence.excerpt: Jokowi asked ministers and related agency heads to stop raising postponement of the 2024 election or extension of his presidential term, saying the process had to stay constitutional.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous reporting of a direct presidential instruction, with explicit constitutional framing.
evidence.period_fit: Exact April 2022 episode on term-extension pressure.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct to Jokowi as president; the remark is his public response to tenure-extension talk.
contrary_evidence: This is relayed through a minister, not a verbatim presidential transcript.
It shows rejection of discussion, not a broader reform agenda.

evidence.claim: Reuters reported that Jokowi tried to rein in speculation that he would stay in office beyond his legally mandated two terms and ordered ministers to stop calling for an extension or election postponement.
evidence.title: Indonesia president seeks to end talk he is angling for a new term
evidence.excerpt: Reuters reported that Jokowi tried to rein in speculation that he would stay in office beyond his legally mandated two terms and ordered ministers to stop calling for an extension or election postponement.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters-sourced report with direct attribution and a clear dated description, though published through a syndication outlet.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct to Jokowi as decision-maker responding to coalition pressure.
contrary_evidence: The same report says he was criticized for an ambiguous stance and did not explicitly rule out staying longer until that point.

evidence.claim: KPU formally adopted PKPU No. 3 of 2022 on the stages and schedule of the 2024 general election on June 9, 2022.
evidence.title: Peraturan KPU Nomor 3 Tahun 2022 tentang Tahapan dan Jadwal Penyelenggaraan Pemilihan Umum Tahun 2024
evidence.excerpt: KPU formally adopted PKPU No. 3 of 2022 on the stages and schedule of the 2024 general election on June 9, 2022.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official election commission legal record with the enactment date and subject matter stated directly.
evidence.period_fit: Exact 2022 institutional scheduling for the next national election.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Institutional rather than personal; relevant because Jokowi governed within this election timetable.
contrary_evidence: A formal schedule does not by itself prove full independence from political pressure.

evidence.claim: KPU stated that the 2024 election date was set for February 14, 2024, and that the first election stages began on June 14, 2022.
evidence.title: Menuju 610 Hari pelaksanaan Pemilu 2024, Hari Ini Tahapan Pemilu 2024 Dimulai
evidence.excerpt: KPU stated that the 2024 election date was set for February 14, 2024, and that the first election stages began on June 14, 2022.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official KPU article with the election date and stage launch stated plainly.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within 2022 and directly relevant to succession timing.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Institutional and indirect, but it confirms the constitutional election timetable Jokowi did not overturn.
contrary_evidence: This shows the schedule was set, not that all actors accepted it without internal pressure.

evidence.claim: Police fired tear gas and water cannon at students protesting a mooted extension of Jokowi’s stay in office, and the same Reuters report said Jokowi had sought to dampen speculation about staying in power longer.
evidence.title: Indonesia police fire tear gas to disperse protest at parliament
evidence.excerpt: Police fired tear gas and water cannon at students protesting a mooted extension of Jokowi’s stay in office, and the same Reuters report said Jokowi had sought to dampen speculation about staying in power longer.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting provides concrete event details and direct links to the term-extension dispute.
evidence.period_fit: Exact April 2022 protest episode around democratic contestability.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect for the police response, direct for Jokowi's public effort to stop extension talk.
contrary_evidence: The protests themselves show active public contestation rather than closed politics.
The coercive response was operationally police-led, not a documented presidential order.

evidence.claim: Freedom House said Indonesia’s electoral framework is largely democratic and electoral authorities are mostly seen as impartial, but activists worry the 2016 consultation requirement with parliament and government could reduce their independence.
evidence.title: Indonesia: Freedom in the World 2023 Country Report
evidence.excerpt: Freedom House said Indonesia’s electoral framework is largely democratic and electoral authorities are mostly seen as impartial, but activists worry the 2016 consultation requirement with parliament and government could reduce their independence.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Annual country report from a major democracy monitor with a clear institutional assessment.
evidence.period_fit: Describes the institutional baseline in force during Jokowi’s 2022 term.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Country-level context rather than direct Jokowi action; useful for separating inherited institutions from ruler conduct.
contrary_evidence: The same passage acknowledges a legal design that may weaken election-body independence.

evidence.claim: Freedom House said women have full political rights, but ethnic Chinese are poorly represented, some local governments discriminate against religious minorities, and LGBT+ people are also poorly represented in politics.
evidence.title: Indonesia: Freedom in the World 2023 Country Report
evidence.excerpt: Freedom House said women have full political rights, but ethnic Chinese are poorly represented, some local governments discriminate against religious minorities, and LGBT+ people are also poorly represented in politics.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Annual country report with a direct statement on political equality and exclusion of several groups.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Country-level structural context; not proof of a 2022 ruler choice, but relevant to the chapter’s equality lens.
contrary_evidence: The report also notes women enjoy full political rights and there are formal gender quotas.

evidence.claim: In June and July 2022, Kominfo required online service providers to register under MR 5/2020 and warned unregistered platforms could be blocked; several platforms were briefly blocked before compliance.
evidence.title: Indonesia: Freedom on the Net 2023 Country Report
evidence.excerpt: In June and July 2022, Kominfo required online service providers to register under MR 5/2020 and warned unregistered platforms could be blocked; several platforms were briefly blocked before compliance.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Country report documents a dated 2022 policy action and its enforcement consequences.
evidence.period_fit: Exact 2022 period and directly relevant to digital political control.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Government-level action under Jokowi’s presidency; not a personal order, but an administrative control within his executive branch.
contrary_evidence: The stated rationale was platform compliance, not explicit political censorship, though the effect still constrained information access.

evidence.claim: Amnesty said two journalists were intimidated while covering the Ferdy Sambo shooting case and argued the repeated intimidation showed the state was still not serious about protecting journalists.
evidence.title: Intimidasi terhadap jurnalis berulang, kebebasan pers harus dilindungi
evidence.excerpt: Amnesty said two journalists were intimidated while covering the Ferdy Sambo shooting case and argued the repeated intimidation showed the state was still not serious about protecting journalists.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous rights-monitoring report with concrete incident details and explicit accountability criticism.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect; the intimidation was carried out by non-state or police-linked actors, but it occurred within Jokowi’s national political environment.
contrary_evidence: The article is advocacy-oriented and does not by itself establish direct presidential direction.

evidence.claim: Amnesty said 2022 civil liberties shrank, the ITE law was used in at least 37 expression cases involving 46 victims, and 11 cases involved virtual police patrols; it also described sustained repression of critics, especially in Papua and Papua Barat.
evidence.title: Catatan Akhir 2022: Suram, Wajah Masa Depan HAM di Indonesia
evidence.excerpt: Amnesty said 2022 civil liberties shrank, the ITE law was used in at least 37 expression cases involving 46 victims, and 11 cases involved virtual police patrols; it also described sustained repression of critics, especially in Papua and Papua Barat.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Year-end rights report with concrete 2022 counts and a clear pattern claim.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but material; the report describes the national political environment under Jokowi and the police/legal apparatus operating in his term.
contrary_evidence: The report combines many incidents and some long-running patterns, so it does not isolate Jokowi’s personal responsibility for every case.

evidence.claim: The new criminal code added offenses for insulting the president or vice president, insulting government or state institutions, and expanded blasphemy restrictions; some offenses require a written complaint from the president or vice president.
evidence.title: Indonesia: New Criminal Code Passed by Parliament
evidence.excerpt: The new criminal code added offenses for insulting the president or vice president, insulting government or state institutions, and expanded blasphemy restrictions; some offenses require a written complaint from the president or vice president.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Law Library summary of the enacted provisions with article-level detail and complaint requirements stated clearly.
evidence.period_fit: Exact December 2022 legal change affecting speech and dissent.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Institutional and indirect; the law was passed by parliament in Jokowi’s term and would affect political speech under his presidency.
contrary_evidence: The law is a legislative act rather than a presidential decree, although the president’s signature and administration would matter for implementation.
